summary: Screen-share preflight previously treated any matching foreground service as ready. It now inspects the installed app's merged ServiceInfo and requires the MediaProjection foreground-service type on Android Q+, before requesting the native capture track. The bundled flutter_background service starts with FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MANIFEST, so the declared service type is applied.

checks.name: Android foreground-service contract before fix
checks.observation: The contract test failed because the readiness poll checked only service.foreground and did not check the MediaProjection service declaration.

checks.name: Android foreground-service contract after fix
checks.observation: The app manifest declaration, MainActivity ServiceInfo preflight, and plugin MANIFEST startup mode are all asserted.

checks.name: Legacy Kotlin Gradle mode
checks.observation: Flutter Android debug APK assembled successfully.

checks.name: AGP built-in Kotlin Gradle mode
checks.observation: The direct Android Gradle debug build completed successfully with JDK 17. The combined verification script's second command initially selected JDK 8 and stopped before compilation; the same mode was rerun with the configured JDK 17.

limitations: The source contract verifies the merged-manifest query and the plugin's MANIFEST startup mode, but the updated client was not installed on Pixel and the guard was not observed at runtime.

This preflight prevents a missing manifest declaration from being mistaken for a ready capture service; it does not explain the previously observed voice participant/publication loss during backgrounding or prove actual MediaProjection persistence.
remaining: Install a fresh Android build only with user authorization, then correlate MediaProjection, foreground-service lifetime, room roster, sender encoded frames and receiver decoded frames across app-background/app-resume. Keep FE-64 open until that device acceptance passes.
